page_hint: Ch 26 §8 Step 2 (Table 26-2 provenance note)
quoted_clause: the ~29% is the same definition at the cached ~1.3 rps engine load (45% x 1.3/2.0 ~ 29%, scaled with engine load)
observed: SM utilization in a decode-bound regime tracks resident-request occupancy, not arrival rate. At the baseline's rho ~ 1 the occupancy is pinned at C = 17.5, so scaling utilization by the rate ratio (0.65) is not the same as scaling by the occupancy ratio; the two coincide only if service time is unchanged, which the chapter elsewhere says it is not (the baseline is queue-inflated). The chapter declares the value as an assumption and says one load test must measure both, but the scaling basis is not named.
evidence: Occupancy at 1.3 rps with the canonical service time is about 1.3 x 8.6 = 11.2, giving an occupancy ratio of 11.2/17.5 = 0.64 against the rate ratio of 0.65 - close here, but the coincidence depends on the unchanged-service-time assumption the chapter elsewhere abandons.
root_cause: The scaling basis was left implicit, so the number's sensitivity to the queue-inflation assumption is invisible.
correction: State the scaling basis explicitly ('scaled with resident-request occupancy, which at unchanged service time is proportional to arrival rate') and note the unchanged-service-time assumption it depends on.
acceptance_test: The provenance note names the quantity the 45% -> 29% scaling is proportional to and states the assumption it depends on.

page_hint: Ch 26 §3 (Pattern B, TTL hypothesis)

observed: The stated reason ('repeat within the same session') explains a higher hit ratio; it says nothing about staleness risk, which is the second and more consequential half of the claim. The chapter elsewhere is careful to separate the two (R-03: 'a TTL never repairs an authorization mismatch'; Table 26-1 tracks 'stale read rate'), so the reasoning here is weaker than the chapter's own standard.
evidence: Table 26-1's Semantic Response Cache FACT set: 'hit ratio @ TTL=T; stale read rate; cache memory pressure'.
root_cause: One hypothesis bundles two claims with one supporting reason.
correction: Split into two testable claims with their own evidence: (a) hit ratio rises to ~55% (reason: session-level repetition), and (b) stale-read rate stays within the Table 26-1 threshold (reason: corpus-version isolation in the key plus a stated staleness budget).
acceptance_test: The TTL hypothesis names a separate acceptance criterion for the stale-read rate, and the reason given for each half matches the claim it supports.
